title: Findings expected
article: Investigators have finished examining the home where Robert Scott Carpenter was shot and killed by an Amherstburg police officer and will likely release their findings in two weeks.

Jon Ansell of the province's Special Investigations Unit said most of the investigation team has returned to Toronto. The lead investigator will remain in Amherstburg to talk with the coroner and conduct any follow-up interviews. Six investigators were dispatched to Carpenter's 258 McCurdy Drive home Monday after he was fatally shot by an unidentified Amherstburg police officer. Carpenter, 37, lived in the home with his common-law wife Lisa Stewart and their two children, Sarah, 3 and Noah, 2.

After receiving a disrupted 911 call, police arrived at the home shortly after 7 a.m. Investigators have released few details about the shooting but a police source said the officers confronted a domestic situation and that Carpenter lunged at one of the officers with a knife.Two officers suffered non-life-threatening injuries in the incident.
